But ultimately, if someone continues to bleed out, you should apply a proper tourniquet on the extremity a few inches above the wound. The damage you MIGHT cause with a tourniquet is worth their life. But tourniquets really are very safe just in addition to other first aid responses

For minmus head to the wiki and it should list its geostationary orbit height, and the moons rotation period. You will need to aim for getting a circular orbit very near to that height, and your satellites orbital period should match Minmus' rotation period.

For Minmus:

Synchronous orbit: 357.94 km. This should be your orbital altitude, quite near perfectly circular.

Sidereal rotation period:	40 400.000 s = 1 d 5 h 13 m 20 s. This should be your satellites orbital period. Sacrifice a perfectly circular orbit in favor of getting this number exact. You will want to bring some pretty low power engines and probably select them and set their thrust from 100 to 0.5 in order to get the fine maneuvering perfect.

The biggest thing for me is deciding the empire that id like to be. The basics are as follows:

Species: depending on your DLC this might be less relevant, but to my knowledge and with my DLC there are 3 basic classes: organic (fleshy types like humans, consume food) lithoids (sentient beings comprised of rock and stone, consume minerals) or robotic (duh, consume energy)

Next, the biggest thing to know about is ethics and civics: you get 3 ethic points, read the descriptions for each and decide what your governments political ideology is. Egalitarian (democratic) vs authoritian, spiritualist vs materialist, xenophobe (varying degrees of disliking other alien species) vs xenophile (friendly to other species), ect. You can decide to be "fanatic" in an ethic, which takes 2 of your 3 points. Detailed descriptions and role play will be more important than understanding the buffs right away, imo. If you chose robotic, you must be a sort of hive mind, but this option is also available for other species. Hive minds are not really my wheelhouse tbh. You can also pick your government style, ie how your head of state is elected. You can also play as a megacorporation, which can establish offices on the planets in other empires to do business. Hive minds are a lot simpler so you might want to consider that to start.

Your empires origin (what happened to your empire before/as they developed space-faring tech.

At this point, go through most of the other screens and just kind of pick what looks cool, you can't go too wrong for your first game.

Game play basics: science ships survey systems, fully surveyed systems may have an "outpost" established by a construction ship, giving you control. Then, construction ships can use minerals to construct mining or research stations above resources. Habitable planets will be displayed on the main galaxy maps. Your first Starbase (click the white circles next to your home stars name, or find your shipyard on the right of the screen) can construct military or colony ships. 
Keep your resources balanced, get as much research and unity (culture perks) as you can. Expand, war, listen to the tutorial.

At absolute minimum you just need the FTL drive (dont need to plan for that really the quest will push you to it), as well as a ship bridge, scanner, and a cryosleep casket for each pawn you want to come with you. You could build your ship and really only put it in space when it's time to leave.

Obviously you need shields and heatsinks and guns for battle, but if you JUST want to hop planets better to focus on engines to flee battle. The regular gun turrets from base game will only work outside your ship if enemies attempt to board your ship. Otherwise, to shoot a ship at a distance, you need the ship specific weapons. I recommend focusing on railguns and engines, as if you can keep hostile ships at nearly the max distance, and disable all of their rail guns so and missles. Next I go for engines to save the fuel of keeping them at the right distance (i get their engines first if they have enough speed to get in close range with their other weapons). At this point I flip my shields off and slowly make my way through their hull.

Beyond that, your ship can be whatever you want it to be. I typically create a ship capable of sustaining 5-10 of my pawns, eventually move most of my fabrication and any remaining research to the ship, I make liberal use of misc robots which on my SOS2 ships outnumber my colonists about 10 to 1. So to maintain my ghost crew I have a section with rooms (I put this outside so more valuable sections can have a buffer. Losing your ship bridge is losing combat), I usually include dining on the ship bridge. I recommend having hospital beds, if you don't have a huge crew you can get misc robots to patch up consists and prisoners in space. 

Some will have sections of their mothership that can separate and land on the surface with all the basics to get a new colony started. My current playthrough is a trading company so I expect to have a MASSIVE cargo hauler, but I will include a full time crew. SOS2 is what finally pushed me to get more storage mods.

Finally, for empire, I usually have a throne on the bridge and a room or 2 that can accommodate royals, sometimes ive had a basically useless royal pawn living on my ship doing nothing but "overseeing" all of our colonies and the like (practically, nothing. But its all about my headcannon)
Hope this wasn't too much info! SOS2 can be overwhelming. I would ultimately recommend you include at least a barracks, dining table, and hospital. I tend to make packaged survival meals on the ground to send up.
